node-1.label: A man in his 40s presented with a 12-month history of nasal swelling

node-2.label: The swelling gradually increased in size since onset, causing pain and right-sided nasal blockage; no discharge, rhinorrhea, or anosmia were reported.

node-3.label: The nasal swelling caused emotional distress due to its prominent appearance, leading to the patient becoming housebound and experiencing social isolation; medical history included anxiety.

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed a prominent cystic swelling on the right side of the external nose with an associated internal component; the swelling was fluctuant, fluid-filled, and tender, and anterior rhinoscopy showed narrowing of the internal nasal valve.

why.why: MRI shows no intracranial connection, and histopathology reveals a benign epithelial cyst with double-layered epithelium and squamous differentiation, confirming the lesion is benign. The chronic 12-month course, fluctuant cystic examination, and absence of acute inflammation or malignant features further support this diagnosis, increasing confidence from 0.65 to 0.95.

Histopathology demonstrates a benign epithelial cyst and excludes acute inflammatory changes. The 12-month course without discharge also argues against an infectious process; tenderness and fluctuance are nonspecific and outweighed by the pathological findings, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.05.

Histopathology confirms a benign epithelial cyst and explicitly excludes neoplasia. MRI shows no intracranial connection, and there are no malignant features such as anosmia or aggressive growth. These findings make a nasal tumor very unlikely, reducing confidence from 0.15 to 0.02.

node-9.label: Histopathology reveals a nasal cyst lined by double-layered epithelium with squamous differentiation and focal corrugated cuticle

node-10.label: Histopathology report states no malignant features or acute inflammatory changes

node-11.label: Benign epithelial cyst of the nasal cavity
